images.title: Change the last two digits
images.purpose: Show that to make 8560 a multiple of 8 we keep 85 and change the last two digits to 52, giving 8552 = 8 × 1069.
images.composition: One row of four big boxes centred high on a white page, one equation line centred below, wide empty space around.
images.exact_structure: One row of exactly 4 equal square boxes holding 8, 5, 5, 2. The first 2 boxes (8 and 5) have a teal #0072B2 outline. The last 2 boxes (5 and 2) are filled amber #E69F00. Below, one grey #6B7280 line of text. Exactly 4 boxes, 1 equation line.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
more or fewer than 4 boxes, or a different digit in any box
images.takeaway: Change only the last two digits to get a multiple of 8.
images.description: The number 8552 as four boxes: 85 kept in teal and the new last two digits 52 in amber, with 8552 = 8 × 1069 below.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at which digits were kept and which were changed.

image_decisions.why: Keeping the front digits and changing the end is a picture idea; one highlighted row carries it.
